blocks.content: Every State shall constitute at the district level a District Planning Committee to consolidate the plans prepared by the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the district and to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.

rows: Consolidates Panchayat & Municipality plans for District
Prepares draft development plan for Metropolitan area

items: Elected proportion trap: DPC requires at least 4/5th elected members, whereas Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC) requires 2/3rd.
Constitutional Amendment: Introduced by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 under Part IX-A, even though it covers rural Panchayats.
Submission Authority: The DPC Chairperson forwards the draft development plan directly to the State Government.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 243ZD mandates the constitution of a District Planning Committee (DPC) at the district level in every state.
Four-fifths (4/5th) of the total members of the DPC are elected by elected members of the district panchayat and municipalities from among themselves.
The representation of rural and urban population in the committee is proportional to the ratio between the rural and urban population of the district.
The DPC consolidates plans prepared by Panchayats and Municipalities to prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.
The Chairperson of the District Planning Committee forwards the consolidated draft development plan to the State Government.
